subject: On-prem / Air-gapped follow-up: hardware, upgrades, offline ops
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Tom Benson <t.benson@legacybank.com>, Sofia Martinez <sofiam@legacybank.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Sep 2028 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & HW checklist for air-gapped deployment

Hi Tom / Sofia,

Thanks again for the productive call today — appreciate you walking us through Legacy Bank's on-prem goals and the constraints around air-gapped operations. Quick recap and suggested next steps: 

- Goal: Run Redwood Private in an on-prem air-gapped environment on dedicated racks for inference workloads (production latency SLOs and local data residency).
- Primary concerns you raised: hardware compatibility, upgrade/patch processes in an offline environment, and maintenance windows (hot vs cold).

Action items we agreed:
1) You to share a hardware inventory (make/model, CPU, GPU type, NIC, disk config) — helps us map to supported driver/kernel combos and recommended minimums.
2) We will send our on-prem hardware checklist and a brief doc on offline upgrade/patch workflows.
3) Schedule a 60-min HW workshop with one of our infra engineers and your IT Ops team to walk the inventory and call out any gaps.
4) Discuss procurement/timing once we confirm the HW profile.

I attached our redwood_onprem_hardware_req.pdf — quick checklist and minimums. Could you share the inventory by EOD Thursday? If that's tight, a sample exported CSV is fine.

Also, two quick clarifications from our side that will help the workshop:
- Do you have any constraints on removable media for patches (e.g., only scanned USBs allowed)?
- Is there an existing DR/backup process for model artifacts and KV caches?

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if easier.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_onprem_hardware_req.pdf (pdf, 120KB)

From: Tom Benson <t.benson@legacybank.com>

Cc: Sofia Martinez <sofiam@legacybank.com>, IT Ops <it-ops@legacybank.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Sep 2028 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & HW checklist for air-gapped deployment

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Attaching our HW inventory export (legacybank_hw_inventory.xlsx). High level:

- GPU fleet: 6x NVIDIA A40 (on older 2U nodes), 2x A100 (on newer 4U nodes)
- CPU: Dual-socket Intel 6338 per node
- Networking: Mellanox ConnectX-6 100Gbps, some nodes have 25Gb for management
- Storage: local NVMe for cache, SAN-backed NFS for artifacts (NFS is on segmented management VLAN)

On offline ops: we have strict policies — removable media is allowed but must be scanned by dedicated bridge systems and approved by security. We prefer scheduled maintenance windows on weekends (Sat 0100–0600 local). DR for model artifacts today is nightly sync to an isolated backup appliance — we can share details in the workshop.

We'll target EOD Thursday for a cleaned-up Excel with serial numbers and OS/kernel versions.

Tom
Director, Platform Engineering
Legacy Bank

Attachment: legacybank_hw_inventory.xlsx (xlsx, 350KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Tom Benson <t.benson@legacybank.com>, Sofia Martinez <sofiam@legacybank.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, IT Ops <it-ops@legacybank.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Sep 2028 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & HW checklist for air-gapped deployment

Tom — this is perfect, thanks. A few notes based on what you shared:

- GPU support: A40s are supported for inference but you'll see better throughput/cost tradeoffs on A100s for larger-batch workloads. We'll call out tuning knobs in the HW workshop.
- Networking: 100Gb Mellanox is great — we'll recommend dedicated NICs for model traffic and separate management paths to preserve the SAN/NFS segmentation you mentioned.
- Storage: local NVMe for KV cache is ideal; for model artifacts we recommend a pull model from the isolated backup appliance during approved maintenance windows.

Offline upgrade/patch approach (summary):
- We support two upgrade modes for air-gapped setups:
  1) Portable-media based installs (signed bundles you import via scanned USB/secure bridge).
  2) Staged internal repo syncs via an approved transfer appliance (you control sync cadence).
- For kernel/driver upgrades that affect GPU drivers, we advise a canary node first and a rollback snapshot for model artifacts + configs.
- Typical maintenance window: 2–4 hours for a coordinated OS/kernel + runtime upgrade (we test in our lab to produce a runbook).

I've attached onprem_install_guide_v2.pdf which includes signed bundle flow and recommended rollback steps. Next steps I propose:
- Schedule HW workshop (60 min) next week — we have slots Tue/Wed 10–12 PT. Can you confirm a time and list attendees?
- We'll prepare a preliminary compatibility matrix from your inventory before the workshop.

Thanks — looping Monica for procurement/timeline coordination.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: onprem_install_guide_v2.pdf (pdf, 540KB)

Hi Tom — thanks for the inventory and Marissa for the guide. A couple items from procurement/schedule side:

- Pricing: We'll prepare a Dedicated vs Private on-prem estimate based on the HW matrix. Private (air-gapped) has a one-time deployment fee + annual support; we'll model both options in the estimate.
- Timeline: once HW is confirmed and workshop is done, typical turnaround for signed-bundle delivery and scoped install is ~4–6 weeks (depends on procurement and access approvals).
- Can you confirm who will be our procurement contact and whether you require a purchase order or DocuSign?

Rishi, looping you to help coordinate the workshop and commercial next steps.

Thanks — Monica
